criteria.guidance: Open each cited file, decision or number. Fail when a cited source doesn't say what the reason claims.
criteria.name: supported
criteria.question: Is every verdict supported by the sources its reason cites?

criteria.guidance: Fail and name the criterion that should have failed or been unsure, with the evidence.
criteria.name: complete
criteria.question: Did the assessment get every criterion right, missing no failure the sources show?

criteria.guidance: Unsure when a verdict rests on taste rather than on something the sources state.
criteria.name: reproducible
criteria.question: Would a second assessor, reading the same sources, reach the same verdicts?

criteria.guidance: Fail when a suggestion improves something else (another rule, the scorecard) but leaves this entity's verdict as it is.
criteria.name: actionable
criteria.question: Would following the suggestions change the verdicts they are attached to?

rubric:seikika/assessment-quality.description: Is this assessment trustworthy? Read the assessment, then the sources its reasons cite, and the entity it judges (seikika get <entity>). Review someone else's assessment, not your own.
rubric:seikika/assessment-quality.name: assessment-quality

criteria.guidance: Fail when the crate docs are missing, stale, or describe several unrelated jobs.
criteria.name: one-responsibility
criteria.question: Does the crate do one thing, stated in its crate docs, that matches its role in docs/v1-spec.md §4?

criteria.guidance: Search other crates for `use <crate>::`; fail when they reach internals or receive third-party types.
criteria.name: small-contract
criteria.question: Do other crates use it through a small, documented public API rather than its internals?

criteria.guidance: Pass when it wraps no third-party default. Fail when a public signature names the default's types, or a caller depends on the default directly (its Cargo.toml), so swapping it would change other crates.
criteria.name: replaceable-defaults
criteria.question: If it wraps a default (cel-rust, OpenFGA, DBOS, Postgres, React), could that default be swapped behind a Seikika-owned contract (charter goal 3)?

criteria.guidance: List the riskiest paths first, then find a test for each; unsure when coverage is only indirect.
criteria.name: tests-match-risk
criteria.question: Are its riskiest paths (parsing, authorization, persistence, protocol handling) tested, not only the easy ones?

rubric:seikika/crate-design.description: Is this crate well designed for its place in Seikika? Read its crate docs, public API and tests, and docs/v1-spec.md §4.
rubric:seikika/crate-design.name: crate-design

criteria.guidance: Fail when an entity could pass while missing the intent (e.g. any test counts as tested), or fail while meeting it.
criteria.name: measures-intent
criteria.question: Does passing the check mean what the rule's name and fix say it means, rather than a proxy that can drift from it?

criteria.guidance: Fail when an empty doc comment, a renamed item, a trivial test or a suppression would pass it.
criteria.name: hard-to-game
criteria.question: Is the cheapest way to pass the rule to do the right thing?

criteria.guidance: Fail when the fix is vague, names the wrong place, or the rule needs data the fix doesn't mention.
criteria.name: fix-leads-to-pass
criteria.question: Would following the fix text alone, with the evidence, make the rule pass?

criteria.guidance: Pass for rules with no threshold. Cite the source; unsure when no source states the number.
criteria.name: threshold-justified
criteria.question: Are its thresholds and its level (bronze, silver or gold) justified by a design doc, a decision or evidence?

rubric:seikika/rule-quality.description: Is this rule a good standard? Read its check, evidence and fix in the portal's seikika.yaml, its tests, and the design doc its scorecard cites.
rubric:seikika/rule-quality.name: rule-quality

criteria.guidance: Fail when its rules serve two audiences or layers (e.g. security and speed); name the split.
criteria.name: one-concern
criteria.question: Does it measure one concern for one audience (one SDLC layer), so its level means one thing?

criteria.guidance: Fail when a level mixes unrelated rules or a gold rule is cheaper than a bronze one.
criteria.name: levels-are-a-ladder
criteria.question: Does each level build on the one below, with bronze reachable now and gold worth reaching?

criteria.guidance: Fail and name the missing rule; compare with the research its design doc cites.
criteria.name: no-obvious-gap
criteria.question: Is there no obvious standard for this concern that the scorecard leaves out?

criteria.guidance: Fail when a rule's fix names no place to change, or it has no evidence; try raising one entity yourself.
criteria.name: actionable
criteria.question: Can an agent raise an entity one level using only the scorecard's fixes, evidence and the portal's tools?

rubric:seikika/scorecard-quality.description: Is this scorecard a good standard? Read it in the portal's seikika.yaml with the doc that motivates it (portal/README.md says which layer it raises).
rubric:seikika/scorecard-quality.name: scorecard-quality

criteria.guidance: Fail when nothing in `checks:` would fail if the exit criterion were not met.
criteria.name: executable-exit
criteria.question: Is the exit criterion checked by a command or CI step, not by judgement?

criteria.guidance: Fail and name the step that needs a person, a secret or tribal knowledge.
criteria.name: agent-can-complete
criteria.question: Could an agent complete the stage using only the listed commands, Seikika's CLI or MCP, and the docs?

criteria.guidance: Fail when consumers compile Seikika or install tools by hand; pass when nothing is built or installed in the stage.
criteria.name: reuses-artifacts
criteria.question: Does the stage reuse released, pinned artifacts instead of rebuilding or reinstalling everything from source?

criteria.guidance: Fail when the stage requires adding a crate, a builtin or a schema change to this repository.
criteria.name: decoupled-from-core
criteria.question: Can someone outside this repository's maintainers carry out the stage (an operator or package author), or does it need a change to Seikika's own crates?

criteria.guidance: Cite the measured time of the stage's fastest gate. Fail when the only gate is a CI run, a release or a person's review, or when no doc measures how long the gate takes.
criteria.name: fast-feedback
criteria.question: Does an agent learn whether its change passes the stage within minutes, from a check it can run locally, before CI or a reviewer?

criteria.guidance: Fail when every check or fixture the stage runs uses one reference, such as only Seikika's own portal, and name it. Pass and name the second reference otherwise, or when the stage produces something with no example to fit, such as a release tag.
criteria.name: beyond-one-reference
criteria.question: Is the stage proven on more than one reference (portal, repository, package or platform), so it cannot pass by fitting one example?

rubric:seikika/sdlc-stage-quality.description: Can this SDLC stage be carried out well, by an agent? Read the stage in portal/sdlc/stages/, its docs and checks, and try its commands.
rubric:seikika/sdlc-stage-quality.name: sdlc-stage-quality

criteria.guidance: Fail when a plausible high-impact regression has no direct test. Cite the case that protects each high-consequence outcome or name the gap.
criteria.name: risk-coverage
criteria.question: Do the tests protect the main case and the highest-risk edge or failure outcomes?

criteria.guidance: Fail when the test can pass despite a wrong result or unintended side effect. Cite the output, state or independent reference it checks.
criteria.name: meaningful-oracles
criteria.question: Do the assertions distinguish correct outcomes from plausible wrong ones?

criteria.guidance: Fail when CI skips the case, suppresses failure, or depends on unprovisioned services. Cite the workflow step and how it runs the case. Mark unsure when the workflow hides execution behind unavailable tooling.
criteria.name: reliable-execution
criteria.question: Will CI exercise these cases with controlled dependencies and visible failures?

rubric:seikika/testing-contract-quality.description: Read the declared contract, implementation, tests and workflow.
rubric:seikika/testing-contract-quality.name: testing-contract-quality

reasons:
fail one-responsibility: The crate docs are stale. They say "snapshot loop + REST API. Later milestones add authorization (M3), MCP, the UI host and connectors (M4)" (crates/seikika-api/src/lib.rs:1-2), and the Cargo description says MCP and the UI "arrive in M4". All of those shipped. The crate now also holds: - the connector runtime: supervision, freshness resyncs, reconciliation (src/connectors.rs:1-4); - action runs with approvals and their own Postgres or file persistence (src/actions.rs:1-30); - assessment briefs (src/assess.rs).
The docs/v1-spec.md:96 row says "axum REST + OpenAPI generation; MCP (rmcp); UI host". There is no OpenAPI generation, MCP is hand-written JSON-RPC rather than rmcp (src/mcp.rs:1-4; no `rmcp` in any Cargo.toml), and the connector runtime the spec gives to seikika-connect (docs/v1-spec.md:94) is here. Neither the docs nor the spec say what this crate is today.

fail small-contract: The intended contract is small and documented: `app_state_with`, `Config` and `serve` (src/lib.rs:23-84). But all eleven modules are `pub` (src/lib.rs:4-15), and the CLI reaches into server modules for logic that has nothing to do with serving: - `connectors::resolve_config` and `connectors::binary_for` (src/connectors.rs:209-219) are used by `seikika report`, `seikika install` and `connector test` (crates/seikika-cli/src/report.rs:162-166, 1445-1446; crates/seikika-cli/src/install.rs:331; crates/seikika-cli/src/main.rs:1126). - `actions::signing_seed`, `actions::approval_key_for` and `actions::served_dir` are used by the offline `seikika run` and by `serve --detach` (crates/seikika-cli/src/run.rs:314, 687; crates/seikika-cli/src/detach.rs:28, 195).
So a checkout-only command links the whole server for config resolution and a key derivation.

fail replaceable-defaults: Reads go through `Arc<dyn Store>` and `Arc<dyn Authorizer>` (src/state.rs:88-94). The UI host serves whatever bundle is in crates/seikika-api/ui-dist, with no React dependency (src/ui.rs:7-9). But the public `app_state_with` and `AppState` take a concrete `Option<seikika_store::PgStore>` next to the trait object (src/lib.rs:24-49; src/state.rs:94). Three things bypass the Store contract: - action-run persistence (`pg.runs`, `put_run`, `put_spent`; src/actions.rs:157-161, 183-195); - snapshot-loop leadership (`pg.try_lead`, src/state.rs:277-279); - a second, file-based backend hand-written inline for the same runs (src/actions.rs:166-199).
Swapping Postgres would change this crate, not just seikika-store.

fail tests-match-risk: There is broad integration coverage: - REST reads and filters (tests/api.rs:34-318); - forge identity refusals (tests/api.rs:320-352); - facet shaping, revocation, hidden-facet probing and snapshot-bound decisions, required in CI (tests/authz.rs:89-322); - every MCP tool (tests/mcp.rs:80-627); - the served action path (scripts/m5-acceptance.sh:108-112).
Three risky server-side guards have no test anywhere: 1. The deletion safety valve, which holds a resync's deletes at ≥90% of a kind (src/connectors.rs:22, 98-131). No test or script matches DELETION_THRESHOLD or "held … deletes". 2. Connector bearer-token authentication (`connector_of`, src/routes.rs:654-671). Every test uses the dev header `x-seikika-connector` (tests/api.rs:48), and nothing sets `connector_tokens`. 3. Rejection of an undeclared connector or record kind (src/connectors.rs:31-50).
`markdown` in src/mcp.rs:619 (complexity 51, 378 lines) is only checked through a few tool outputs.
suggestions: one-responsibility: Rewrite lib.rs's doc to name the crate's actual job ("the served portal: REST, MCP, UI host, connector runtime and action runs over one AppState") and list its modules. Update the Cargo description and the v1-spec §4 rows for seikika-api and seikika-connect (or record a decision) so OpenAPI, rmcp and the connector runtime's home match the code.

small-contract: Move `resolve_config` and `binary_for` to seikika-connect, or to seikika-model next to `artifacts`. Move `signing_seed` and `approval_key_for` to seikika-exec's `grant` module. Make the remaining modules `pub(crate)`, except what tests and `serve` need.

replaceable-defaults: Add run records, spent tokens and the leader lease to the `Store` trait, or to a small `RunStore` trait with Postgres and file implementations in seikika-store. Then hold only trait objects in `AppState`, and drop `pg: Option<PgStore>` from `app_state_with`.

tests-match-risk: Add API tests: - ingest N records, then resync with none, and assert the deletes are held; then resync with N-1 and assert one delete; - configure a connector token and assert 401 without it, 401 with another connector's token, and 202 with its own; - post a record of an undeclared kind and assert 422 `invalid-messages`; - post as an undeclared connector and assert 403.
fields.summary: The served-portal crate has good end-to-end tests for reads, authorization and MCP. Its design has drifted, though. The crate docs and spec row predate M4 and M5. Every module is public, and offline CLI commands reach into it. Run persistence bypasses the Store trait through a concrete PgStore. The guards that protect data on ingest (the deletion safety valve, connector tokens, kind scoping) are untested.

reasons:
pass one-responsibility: Who is calling, and what may they do. The crate docs list five modules, all serving that one question (crates/seikika-authz/src/lib.rs:1-8): - `authn`: IAP, OIDC, PAT and dev identity; - the `Authorizer` contract with its OpenFGA co-process; - `fga_dsl`, which compiles the model language; - `fgatest`, which runs `.fga.yaml` tests; - `local`, which checks against tuples with no server.
That is the docs/v1-spec.md:92 row and D38. The spec row also names "facet shaping; audit", but facet shaping lives in seikika-api (crates/seikika-api/src/access.rs:289), so the row overstates this crate rather than the crate doing too much.

pass small-contract: seikika-api holds the authorizer only as `Arc<dyn Authorizer>` (crates/seikika-api/src/state.rs:90). Beyond that it uses `Tuple`, `authn::Authenticator` and `fga_dsl::has_relation` (crates/seikika-api/src/access.rs:9-10, 86). seikika-cli is the composition root: it calls `OpenFga::start`, `install_tuple_view`, `fga_dsl::to_json`, `local::Local`, `fgatest::run_file` and the PAT helpers (crates/seikika-cli/src/server.rs:61-92, 415-423). All of these are module-level public functions, not internals. One weakness: 12 of 36 public items lack docs, including `Authenticator`, `AuthConfig`, `AuthError`, `Mode`, `Tuple` and `Datastore` (src/authn.rs:23-160, src/openfga.rs:12-14), the types callers construct.

pass replaceable-defaults: OpenFGA sits behind the Seikika-owned `Authorizer` trait (src/lib.rs:18-34). The API never names `OpenFga` (crates/seikika-api/src/state.rs:90), and packaging stays swappable as D38 and Q11 intend. Rough edges, none of which put an OpenFGA type in a caller: - `install_tuple_view` takes `&sqlx::PgPool` (src/openfga.rs:414), which seikika-cli takes from PgStore's public `pool` field (crates/seikika-cli/src/server.rs:89-90). - `sync_tuples`'s contract documents the Postgres-view implementation's behaviour (src/lib.rs:31-33). - `Authorizer::model` returns OpenFGA's model JSON, which seikika-api reads through `fga_dsl::has_relation`.

unsure tests-match-risk: Several high-risk paths have direct tests: - authn: ES256 IAP JWTs, RS256 OIDC with rejections, PATs and dev headers, and token mode ignoring the dev header (tests/authn.rs:57-161); - the DSL compiler, checked against the fga CLI's JSON for every operator (tests/fga.rs:15-50); - the reference `.fga.yaml` through the Authorizer, required in CI via SEIKIKA_REQUIRE_OPENFGA (tests/fga.rs:60-68); - batch errors not being denials (src/openfga.rs:499).
Two security-relevant paths are only covered indirectly: - `local::Local` claims it "never grants more than the server's OpenFGA would" (src/local.rs:1-6). It has four hand-written cases (src/local.rs:145-200) but no differential run against OpenFGA on the same model and tuples. - The tuple view's `user_type` mapping (src/openfga.rs:405-413) is exercised only by scripts/m3-acceptance.sh and m4-acceptance.sh. A wrong label there caused intermittent wrong denials that unit tests didn't catch (docs/research-log.md:99).
suggestions: tests-match-risk: Run the reference examples/reference-portal/authz/model.fga.yaml cases through `Local` as well as OpenFGA and assert they agree wherever `Local` answers. Add a unit test of `tuple_view_sql` (or of the user_type CASE) for a plain user, a userset, `*` and `type:*`.
fields.summary: A coherent authn and authz crate, with OpenFGA behind a Seikika-owned trait that the API holds as a trait object. The decided tuple view ties it to Postgres. Authentication and the DSL compiler are well tested. The offline `Local` checker's "never grants more" claim and the tuple view's labelling have no direct test, and the latter has already failed once.

fields.summary: The control-channel core (hub, SDK, conformance kit) is the right shape, and every connector uses a narrow SDK surface. The crate has also become a home for unrelated helpers (assessments, file globbing, date formatting). Its central types are undocumented. The spec row's "error mapping to `unknown`" is done by the caller (seikika-derive), not here. That is the right place, but the spec row doesn't say so.

pass small-contract: Every caller uses re-exported, documented items only: seikika-model imports Site and calls check, matching on CelIssue (crates/seikika-model/src/validate.rs:13, 812-816). seikika-derive uses Expr, ExprValue, Scope, with_vals, with_vars and lazy_map (crates/seikika-derive/src/lib.rs:15) and Env (testing.rs:10). seikika-exec uses Expr, ExprValue and with_vars (crates/seikika-exec/src/check.rs:8). seikika-api uses those three and analysis::required_equalities, whose input and output are strings (crates/seikika-api/src/routes.rs:17, 218). seikika-cli calls analysis::analyse (crates/seikika-cli/src/meta.rs:183, model.rs:28, 160). Errors cross as String (eval.rs:234), and no caller matches on cel's message text: a search for cel error strings outside the crate finds none. The one rough edge is `Expr::source`, a public field with no doc comment (eval.rs:203).

pass replaceable-defaults: Only this crate depends on cel-rust (crates/seikika-expr/Cargo.toml:11). Apart from the workspace pin (Cargo.toml:22), no other Cargo.toml names `cel`. The crate docs state the contract (lib.rs:16-17). No public signature names a cel type: ExprValue and Lazy keep their cel values in pub(crate) fields (eval.rs:13, 111), Scope wraps a cel Context in a private field (eval.rs:107), and analysis returns Seikika structs or strings (analysis.rs:13-30, 153). Swapping cel-rust would change this crate only.

pass tests-match-risk: The riskiest paths are: 1. JSON-to-CEL conversion, which every score goes through; 2. lazy `inbound` lists; 3. check(), which validate trusts; 4. the per-site variable table; 5. required_equalities, which the API uses to narrow a list, so a wrong result would hide entities the filter accepts.
Each has a direct test, and all 14 pass under `cargo test -p seikika-expr`: - Conversion: u64 above i64::MAX, floats, int compared with double, non-finite floats, a value with no JSON form, and a one-line compile error (eval.rs:338-360). Non-string map keys (eval.rs:284-291), and round trips (eval.rs:293-312). - Lazy lists: size, iteration, indexing, out of bounds, and a string or negative index (eval.rs:249-282). - Env functions and their errors (eval.rs:314-336). - check(): the variable, syntax and undeclared-function branches (lib.rs:168-197). - required_equalities: both operand orders under `&&`, and refusing `||`, `!`, a non-literal, a number, a nested field, has() and invalid CEL (analysis.rs:190-212).
The previous gap is closed. only_a_postcondition_reads_the_executor_outputs (lib.rs:199-215) accepts `outputs` at Site::Postcondition and rejects it at Site::Action with the exact allowed list. seikika-model sends `expect.postcondition` to that site (validate.rs:779-783).
What remains is minor: - The Tuples and ContextLookup variable lists are only exercised positively, through the reference portal (examples/reference-portal/ seikika.yaml:237 and its `candidate.` lookups). - The table and the variables that callers actually bind live in different crates (seikika-exec check.rs:108-116, 193-200), and no test ties them together. - cel-rust itself has not been checked against the CEL spec (Q10, docs/questions.md).
suggestions: tests-match-risk: Add one table-driven test that checks, for each Site, that a variable from another site is rejected. Run a slice of the cel-spec conformance suite through Expr (Q10) and record the result in docs/research-log.md.
fields.summary: The crate does one job, through a small documented contract, with cel-rust fully behind it. The new caller, seikika-exec, uses only the public evaluation API. The new test pins that `outputs` is readable at Site::Postcondition and rejected at Site::Action, which closes the gap a previous draft left `unsure`. What stays open is minor: the Tuples and ContextLookup variable lists have no negative tests, and CEL conformance (Q10) is unmeasured.

reasons: pass risk-coverage: scripts/m5-acceptance.sh exercises a successful approved write, two unauthorized approvers, an explicit rejection, and a push refused by a local origin hook.
pass meaningful-oracles: scripts/m5-acceptance.sh checks the landed file and verification response for success. A refused push must also leave the origin's main ref at its original commit.

pass reliable-execution: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs scripts/m5-acceptance.sh in its acceptance job. The script creates disposable Git origins and local servers, checks command outcomes, and cleans up on exit.
pass risk-coverage: crates/seikika-derive/tests/reference.rs checks reference bytes, reordered input and concrete plan edits. It now asserts that equivalent recomputes yield an empty plan.
pass meaningful-oracles: crates/seikika-derive/tests/reference.rs pins the complete five-file output set and compares bytes against examples/reference-portal/tools/reference.py's fixtures.
pass reliable-execution: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the Rust integration suite and independently regenerates and checks the reference model with pinned Python dependencies.

pass risk-coverage: crates/seikika-cli/tests/ratchet.rs covers new failures, growing evidence, existing debt, and unknown evidence. It also asserts that advisory failures remain visible without blocking the gate and that explicit skips preserve unknown evidence.
pass meaningful-oracles: crates/seikika-cli/tests/ratchet.rs checks exit codes, stable verdict reasons, the exact new evidence, and whether the baseline write was refused.
pass reliable-execution: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs cargo test --locked. The cases in crates/seikika-cli/tests/ratchet.rs use isolated fixture portals and the built binary.

meta-assessment.description: What every assessment must contain to be worth reading: a named assessor, suggestions for findings and citations that resolve in the repository (D80).
meta-assessment.rationale: Agents act on assessments and review cards read them, so a malformed one misleads twice: a finding without a suggestion can't be acted on, and a reason without a citation can't be checked. Bronze is the ratcheted floor every new assessment must meet; silver and gold ask for citations, first on findings, then on every verdict.

assessor-named.fix: Set `assessor.name` to the agent harness or person who made the assessment.
assessor-named.rationale: An unnamed assessment can't be weighed or challenged, and review-assessment needs the name to tell an independent review from a self-review.

cites-everything.fix: Cite a source in every listed reason, passes included, in the same forms as cites-for-findings (a path, a unique file name, an existing decision or question id, a URL), so a reviewer can check the verdict.
cites-everything.rationale: A pass is a claim too; without a citation a reviewer can't tell a checked pass from a guess, and a wrong pass hides a problem the assessment was meant to find.

cites-for-findings.check: entity.uncited.filter(c, c in entity.failing || c in entity.unsure).size() == 0
cites-for-findings.fix: In the assessment file under portal/assessments/, cite what each listed fail or unsure reason rests on, in a form a reader can open: a repository path (`crates/x/src/lib.rs:40`), a file name only one file has, a decision or question id that exists (D71, Q10), or a full URL. A section sign or a bare number alone isn't checkable.
cites-for-findings.rationale: A finding that cites nothing a reader can open can be neither verified nor disputed; on the first run, 6 of 9 assessments fell below silver because their reasons named a behaviour without a path or a number.

suggests-fixes.fix: Add a `suggestion:` to each listed fail or unsure verdict: the change that would make it pass.
suggests-fixes.rationale: A fail or unsure verdict with no suggested change leaves the reader to rediscover the fix, so the finding tends to go unacted.

meta-assessment.title: Assessments are well-formed

meta-rubric.description: Each rubric agents judge with: described, used, guided with what counts as fail, and shown to discriminate on real assessments (D80).
meta-rubric.rationale: A rubric decides what agents judge, so a vague one yields reviews that disagree or pass everything. Described and used once is the floor for a new rubric; guidance on what counts as fail lets assessors agree; gold needs three assessments to show that each criterion can fail.

described.fix: Describe what the rubric judges and which sources the assessor should read.
described.rationale: The assessor reads the description to learn what to judge and which sources to read; without it, two assessors judge different things.

discriminates.fix: Sharpen or drop a criterion that everything passes; a question nothing fails asks nothing.
discriminates.rationale: A criterion every assessment passes costs assessor effort and tells nothing apart: `rule-quality`'s `fix-leads-to-pass` passed all four of its first rule assessments.

guided.fix: Give each listed criterion `guidance:` saying what counts as fail, so assessors agree.
guided.rationale: Without guidance on what counts as fail, assessors draw the line in different places and their verdicts can't be compared. Blank guidance used to pass (D01M831P5QWJQ4A2FT85N5MXJQF).

in-use.fix: Assess one entity with it (`seikika assess brief <id> --rubric <name>`), or remove the rubric.
in-use.rationale: A rubric no assessment has used is untried configuration: nobody knows whether its questions can be answered from the sources it names.

meta-rubric.title: Rubrics are well-formed

review-assessment.description: Each assessment reviewed against assessment-quality by another assessor, advisory; reviews of reviews are not made (D80, D01M831P5QWJQ4A2FT85N5MXJQF).
review-assessment.rationale: A deterministic check sees that an assessment cites something, not that the source says what the reason claims; a second assessor's review checks that. Reviews stop at one level, so assessments made with assessment-quality are skipped, and the card is advisory because a review goes stale on every edit.

assessed.fix: Run `seikika assess brief <assessment id> --portal portal`; a different agent or person should review it.
assessed.rationale: A review by the assessment's own assessor repeats its blind spots and is no independent check; one of the first three assessment reviews was a self-review.

no-doubts.fix: Resolve what the reviewer was unsure of, usually by citing the source a verdict rests on.
no-doubts.rationale: A reviewer's doubt usually means a verdict rests on taste rather than a cited source, so a second assessor reading the same sources might reach a different one.

no-open-findings.fix: A current assessment-quality assessment failed the listed criteria: act on its suggestions (portal/assessments/), then re-assess. If the finding is wrong, say why in a new assessment by another assessor.
no-open-findings.rationale: Failing reviews were lost among the unreviewed lines and went unacted for days; putting the assessment at none makes an open finding head the report until it is fixed or disputed.

passes-review.fix: For a listed criterion, revise the assessment file in portal/assessments/ where the review found it unsupported or incomplete, then have it reviewed again. For an item marked "fix the review", the review file is at fault: its reasons must cite what they rest on, including this assessment's file or the sources it cites.
passes-review.rationale: Gold means an independent reviewer checked the assessment against its own sources and found it sound; a review that cites only unrelated files can't have checked it.
